answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting Rule. Each identity’s action sequence is hashed into an onyx ledger per epoch. A new identity must match a prior behavioural profile across three epochs within tolerance, else it waits at a jetty checkpoint before transacting. Enforcement: mismatched fingerprints trigger freeze until 50 verified actions replay the profile. Attackers pay the full compute and time cost of replicating consistent histories for every duplicate, never amortized across the garden of clones.
